$comment: Where a clip's trim edge may go: [lo, hi] in source seconds. gui/web/src/edit/trimLimits.ts trimEdgeLimits mirrors edits/clips_ops.trim_edge_limits, and every client clamp (a held strip nudge, a handle drag, a ripple peer) reads it. gui/web/src/edit/trimLimits.test.ts and tests/test_trim_edge_limits_contract.py both read these cases. Clips are [id, timeline_start, source_start, source_end, source_id] on the case's track (default host), source_id null = the track's own media. A clip with no source_id plays the track media; a clip with one plays that source. Two clips play the same recording when their source_id matches or their files do (the host_t1 source is the host track's media file).

cases.name: a lone clip's end may reach the end of its media
a lone clip's start may reach the start of its media
an end stops at the next clip's start in the same recording
an end does not stop at the next clip's start in another recording
an end stops at the end of its own source, not the track's media
a start stops at the previous clip's end in the same recording
a start does not stop at the previous clip's end in another recording
a source over the track's own media file is the same recording as that media
two clips of one source share its recording
an unmeasured source may not grow past the clip's current end
unmeasured track media may not grow past the clip's current end
a gap end also stops at the next clip on the timeline
a gap end with nothing after it reaches the end of its media
a gap end that touches the next clip cannot grow
a gap start also stops at the previous clip on the timeline
a gap start keeps the previous clip's source end when that is later
a gap start with nothing before it stops at the timeline's start
